context: Current closing price of Lam Research (LRCX): $394.14 USD as of 2026-06-25.
justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a modestly upward-drifting baseline from what I infer was a starting level near 394–396. At the one-day horizon, I anchored closely to the prevailing level because intraday mean reversion tends to dominate over very short windows, and there was little reason to expect an abrupt directional move absent a specific catalyst. For the one-week estimate, I nudged the figure slightly higher to around 400, reflecting a mild bullish drift assumption consistent with the long-run historical tendency of equity indices to trend upward over time, while acknowledging that a week is still short enough that noise dominates signal. At the one-month horizon, I extended that drift further to around 410, roughly consistent with annualized return assumptions in the 6–8% range applied over a single month, treating that as the central tendency in the absence of strong macro signals pulling strongly in either direction.

The confidence interval widths were calibrated to typical realized volatility for a broad equity index. At the one-day level, historical daily moves of roughly 0.5–1% standard deviation justified a tight band of about plus or minus 15 points around the estimate. Over one week, volatility scales by roughly the square root of five, widening the band to around plus or minus 30 points. Over one month, further scaling and the compounding of uncertainty around economic conditions, earnings, and monetary policy pushed the interval to roughly plus or minus 65 points, reflecting both statistical volatility scaling and the growing importance of fundamental uncertainty over longer horizons.

Several specific risks could push outcomes outside these stated intervals. On the downside, a sudden shift in Federal Reserve communication, a significant deterioration in macroeconomic data such as a jobs report or inflation surprise, or an unexpected geopolitical escalation could easily produce moves beyond the 90% bounds, particularly at the one-week and one-month horizons. On the upside, a surprisingly strong earnings season, a dovish policy pivot, or a rapid de-escalation of geopolitical tensions could drive the index well above the upper bounds. The one-month interval is especially susceptible to these tail events because there are simply more scheduled data releases and policy meetings within that window, any one of which could shift the prevailing narrative materially and render the stated range too narrow in hindsight.
